record.title: Combined Compose service identity can carry platform authority into the demo image
record.description: Source review confirms the documented combined launch (docs/DEMO.md:20) lists deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml before deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml, and both files declare services.api under the same project name graveshift. Under standard Compose multi-file merge semantics (not locally rendered in this review), the later demo definition sets image, build.context and x-app environment/networks but does not use !reset or !override (no such directives exist in deploy/compose/), so the platform api definition's environment keys (internal tokens, OAuth JWT secret, root-bootstrap fields at graveshift.compose.yml:94-100), build.dockerfile, command, profiles and core network are not cleared by source. A concrete lower-trust principal exists: .kiro/agents/chaos-witch.json:9 denies shell and denies fs_write except under examples/**, so it can alter the example build context, Dockerfile and launcher but not deploy/platform source. The candidate does NOT assert that the unchanged combination leaks secrets: the retained platform command src/main.ts and build.dockerfile deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile are absent from the example context (verified: no examples/haunted-candy-shop/src/main.ts and no examples/haunted-candy-shop/deploy/), the retained api profile is not enabled by the documented command, and no rendering, build or process execution was permitted. Delivery of a dummy platform-secret marker to an examples-controlled image therefore remains an unobserved, owner/conditional result and is kept as needs_validation.
record.claimed_root_cause: deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml and deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml assign different trust roles to the same Compose service key api. The later demo definition overrides image and build.context but, in source, contains no environment/network/profile/command/build.dockerfile reset directives, so under standard Compose merge the platform API's credential environment, core network, api profile, src/main.ts command and deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile path can be retained. An actor with write authority confined to examples/** can then control the selected image's build and runtime inputs without editing platform configuration. The source-visible prerequisites (api profile co-enablement, nonempty owner credentials, and a runnable examples-supplied variant supplying the absent Dockerfile/entrypoint) are not established as met.

trace.description: Line 9 denies shell and denies fs_write on ** with exclude examples/**; the agent prompt at line 12 restates 'Write only under examples/' and 'Never touch source packages.' This is a concrete lower-trust source-editing role for the example Dockerfile and launcher; the candidate also covers any equivalently scoped example contributor.

Line 5 copies src into the image; line 8 sets CMD bun src/api-main.ts. An examples-only writer controls the code packaged into this lower-trust image and can add examples-local files (e.g. src/main.ts and a compatible deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile under the example context) matching fields retained by the merged service, with no platform-source edit.

services.api (line 78) is opt-in via profiles: [api] (line 82), builds from deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile (line 85), runs bun src/main.ts (line 88), holds internal-token/JWT/root-bootstrap environment fields (lines 94-100, all ${VAR:-} defaults) and joins core (line 105). Empty defaults and the profile gate are material prerequisites, not an observed grant.

Line 20 documents 'docker compose -f deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml -f deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml up -d --build', selecting support first and demo second so same-named service definitions merge; line 81 repeats the order for down. The command does not pass --profile api, so the inherited API profile must be enabled separately for the colliding service to run.

trace.scope: Merged api workload identity and environment
trace.description: services.api (line 23) merges <<: *app (line 24): example build context and haunted-candy-shop:local image (lines 7-9), candy network (line 15), demo environment map (lines 16-20). No reset directives clear the platform fields from the earlier file. The claimed minimum boundary result is a runnable lower-trust image receiving a dummy platform-secret marker; retained core membership is a second configuration effect, without assuming any successful management operation.

evidence.description: fs_write deny on ** with exclude examples/** and shell deny on line 8 supply the limited example-editing role rather than assuming deploy-file write access; line 12 prompt reinforces the scope.
The platform API retains profiles: [api]; a combined run without this profile does not establish execution of the colliding API service, and the documented command at DEMO.md:20 omits it.

build.dockerfile is deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile, which a context-only override retains under the example build context. Verified absent from the current example tree, so the unchanged combination is not established buildable.
command invokes bun src/main.ts. The example provides api-main.ts and worker-main.ts but no src/main.ts, so an unchanged runnable leak is not established.

API environment contains GRAVESHIFT_API_INTERNAL_TOKEN, plus GRAVESHIFT_DAEMON_INTERNAL_TOKEN (95), GRAVESHIFT_OAUTH_JWT_SECRET (96) and root-bootstrap fields (97-100), all sourced from the owner environment with empty defaults. No real values were read or copied.
The platform API joins core, the network shared by the read proxy, broker, database, actuator and Prometheus. The demo override does not explicitly reset this network list.
x-app sets build.context to ../../examples/haunted-candy-shop (line 8), image haunted-candy-shop:local (line 9), networks [candy] (line 15) and a demo environment map (lines 16-20).

The demo uses the identical api service key with <<: *app and no environment/network/profile/command reset or !reset/!override tag (verified none in deploy/compose), supplying the source-visible conflicting handoff.

The normal example launcher consumes process.env via createApi({ env: process.env }); an examples-controlled compatible launcher likewise reads the environment delivered to its container. Actual delivery of a dummy privileged marker remains untested.

The combined support-first, demo-second invocation is maintained documentation (also line 81). Its default profile omission and inherited build/command failures must be accounted for when evaluating applicability.

blockers: No target configuration rendering, image build or process execution was performed: the parent-approved OS sandbox lacks complete memory and cumulative disk controls, and the promotion allowlist is empty. There is no local observed boundary result or retained execution artifact; Compose merge behavior at the effective version is reasoned from standard semantics, not observed locally.

No owner-observed effective Compose version, file order, profile selection or nonempty platform-credential attachment is available. The documented combined command omits --profile api and the platform fields default empty, so an inactive API service or empty credentials do not demonstrate disclosure.

The current unchanged combination is not established runnable: the example context lacks the retained deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile and src/main.ts entrypoint (both verified absent). An examples-only writer can supply compatible files within the declared scope, but that conditional variant has not been exercised; a failed unmodified deployment must not be reported as a live secret leak.

validation_plan.local: In a fully approved OS sandbox with empty allowlisted environment, no external network, read-only target/tooling and scratch-only bounded writes, render the two maintained manifests in the documented order with the api profile enabled from a scratch working directory that has no .env and a minimal explicit environment (env -i) containing only dummy NATS variables and a dummy 32-character platform-secret marker. Inspect only effective services.api image, build context/dockerfile, command, profiles, environment key/marker presence and networks. Determine whether the haunted-candy-shop image and the dummy marker/core network coexist. Account for the absent retained Dockerfile and main.ts; if process-level proof is necessary, use an offline fixture adding only compatible files beneath a scratch examples/ tree and emitting only the dummy marker. Stop at delivery of that marker, or reject the candidate if the supported Compose behavior prevents the handoff. Never build against a registry, use real credentials, contact a live service or inspect unrelated environment values.
validation_plan.deployment: An owner can inspect the effective local deployment definition and launch configuration to establish whether both files are combined in support-first/demo-second order, the api profile is enabled, the example image is runnable and any platform credential fields are nonempty. Record only source/image identity, field names, presence booleans and network membership; do not export secret values or probe live control-plane endpoints. If the image cannot start or the example and platform credentials are never co-enabled, record the candidate as inapplicable to that deployment.
